identity.description: GitHub: a software development platform (git hosting, issues, pull requests, Actions, Copilot). The REST API docs at docs.github.com are its official reference.
identity.identity_notes: The docs.github.com REST docs and the github/github-mcp-server repo (owner github, described as GitHub's official MCP server) are consistent with the product named.

auth.oauth_flows: OAuth apps and GitHub Apps (user-to-server tokens). The MCP GA changelog says the remote server uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.
auth.token_refresh: GitHub App user tokens can be refreshed; the MCP changelog mentions automatic token refresh and short-lived credentials for the remote server. Refresh details for other flows were not fetched.
auth.scopes_notes: Fine-grained PATs use per-endpoint permissions. Classic PATs use scopes. GitHub Apps use installation tokens.

access.production_restrictions: Fine-grained PATs can be set to require organization owner approval; until approved, a token can only read public resources. Organizations can also restrict classic PATs. Test against a personal account or a test org to avoid this.

read_ops: Repository, issue, pull request, user, organization, and Actions resources (per MCP toolsets; REST reference not fetched directly)
write_ops: Create/update issues and pull requests (inferred from MCP toolsets; REST reference not fetched directly)
api.rate_limits: unknown (authenticated requests get a higher limit per the authentication page; exact numbers not verified)
api.limitations: Rate limit figures were not established from the fetched pages. The REST overview page did not state rate limits or pagination. Org-owned resources may require org approval for fine-grained PATs. Webhooks are configured per repository, organization, or GitHub App.

claims.value: GitHub is a developer platform; docs.github.com/en/rest is its REST API reference.
claims.quote: If you want to use the GitHub REST API for personal use, you can create a personal access token.

claims.value: Personal access tokens (fine-grained and classic) are supported.
claims.quote: Fine-grained tokens are preferred. Their access depends on per-endpoint permissions
claims.verify_note: quote not found in fetched source text

claims.value: GitHub Apps are recommended for organization or delegated use; OAuth app tokens are allowed.
claims.quote: If you want to use the API for an organization or on behalf of another user, GitHub recommends that you use a GitHub App.

claims.value: Some GitHub App and OAuth app endpoints require basic authentication with client ID and secret.
claims.quote: Some REST API endpoints for GitHub Apps and OAuth apps require you to use basic authentication to access the endpoint.

claims.value: Username and password authentication is not supported.
claims.quote: Authentication with username and password is not supported.

claims.value: A personal access token can be created by a user; no paid plan is mentioned for the basic PAT flow, and free-plan eligibility is not stated.
claims.quote: Verify your email address, if it hasn't been verified yet.

claims.value: Organization owners can require approval for fine-grained PATs; pending tokens only read public resources until approved.
claims.quote: Organization owners can require approval for any fine-grained personal access tokens

claims.value: Organization owners can restrict classic PATs to their organization.
claims.quote: Organization owners can set a policy to restrict the access of personal access tokens (classic) to their organization.

claims.value: Webhooks are supported; they can be created within a repository, organization, or GitHub App.
claims.quote: Webhooks provide a way for notifications to be delivered to an external web server whenever certain events occur on GitHub.

claims.value: REST and GraphQL APIs are both available.
claims.quote: The Octokit client can be used to send requests to GitHub's REST API and queries to GitHub's GraphQL API.

claims.value: The REST API is versioned by a calendar-based header, X-GitHub-Api-Version; latest version 2026-03-10.
claims.quote: The REST API is now versioned. For more information, see "About API versioning."

claims.value: Octokit is GitHub's all-batteries-included SDK for Browsers, Node.js, and Deno; it covers REST and GraphQL.
claims.quote: The all-batteries-included GitHub SDK for Browsers, Node.js, and Deno.

claims.value: github/github-mcp-server is GitHub's official MCP server, owned by the github organization.
A remote GitHub MCP Server is hosted by GitHub and is generally available.
claims.quote: The remote GitHub MCP Server is hosted by GitHub and provides the easiest method for getting up and running.

claims.value: The remote MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, and a PAT can also be used with the local server.
claims.quote: The GitHub MCP Server now supports OAuth 2.1 + PKCE

claims.value: Community MCP servers exist, e.g. steinybot/github-mcp-server and nickytonline/github-mcp-http.
